citations.locator: Lecture 18, physical PDF page 550, printed slide 7: Independent freedoms and task redundancy
citations.evidenceText:
Number of degrees of freedom (DOF)

•  Arbitrary Pose: To position and orient an end-effector at any specific point in
   3D space, a total of six degrees of freedom are generally required (3 for
    position, 3 for orientation).
•  Task Matching: A design should provide only the DOF required by the task to
   maintain efficiency and cost-effectiveness.
•  Redundancy: A manipulator is redundant for a task if it has more DOF than
   needed.
•  For example, a 6-DOF robot is redundant when using a
   symmetric tool (like a grinding wheel or welding torch)
   because rotation about the tool's axis is redundant.

citations.locator: Lecture 18, physical PDF page 552, printed slide 9: Load rating and configuration dependence
citations.evidenceText:
Load capacity

•  Load capacity is the maximum weight the manipulator can carry throughout its
   workspace while maintaining performance.
•  Factors: It depends on the structural sizing of links, the power-transmission
   system (gears, belts), and the torque/force output of the actuators.
•  Configuration Dependency: Load capacity is not a constant; it is a function of
   the manipulator's configuration (e.g., a fully extended arm supports less weight
   than a retracted one).

•  Dynamic Loading: Design must account for inertial and
   velocity-related forces during high-speed movements,
   not just static weight.





                                                                                                           9

solution.justification: A guarantee over all configurations must respect each configuration’s allowable load. From the given pair it cannot exceed 7 kg, and untested configurations may impose a tighter bound.

optionExplanations.o1: That is a best-configuration capacity, not a whole-workspace guarantee.
optionExplanations.o2: An average does not satisfy the lower-capacity configuration.
optionExplanations.o3: Improving geometric parameter accuracy does not remove configuration-dependent leverage or structural limits.
optionExplanations.o4: A whole-workspace guarantee cannot exceed the weakest evaluated configuration.

citations.evidenceText:
Repeatability and accuracy

•  Repeatability: The ability of the robot to return to the same previously taught
   point.
•  Accuracy: The ability of the robot to move to a mathematically defined point in
   space.
•  Design Trade-off: High precision is expensive. Designers must match the
   robot's precision to the task requirements (e.g., a paint-spraying robot does not
   need 0.001-inch accuracy if the spray spot diameter is 8 ± 2 inches).
 •  Manufacturing vs. Design: Accuracy is often achieved
    through precise manufacturing tolerances and a
    thorough understanding of link parameters (kinematic
    calibration), rather than solely through basic mechanical
    design.

    calibration), rather than solely through basic mechanical
    design.

Number of degrees of freedom (DOF)

•  Arbitrary Pose: To position and orient an end-effector at any specific point in
   3D space, a total of six degrees of freedom are generally required (3 for
    position, 3 for orientation).

   maintain efficiency and cost-effectiveness.

   needed.

   symmetric tool (like a grinding wheel or welding torch)
